newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee open called sharply down after NY.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee open called sharply down after NY.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures were expected to open sharply lower on Monday after frantic speculative selling hammered New York lower by 12 percent on Friday, but expectations of the open varied enormously.

One trader said London could open as much as $500 lower based on a theoretical calculation after the New York slump but other traders said an open of between $200 and $250 down was perhaps more likely.
New York's explosive three-day rally came to an abrupt halt on Friday as July arabicas tumbled 38.40 cents/lb to 276.40 cents in what the CSCE said was coffee's largest one-day decline on record.

But technical analysts said while the market would certainly open lower, the extent of the fall might be confined to a chart gap between $2,262 and $2,360, the lower end of which was around $200 below Friday's close.
"If that gap were to hold, you could probably see the market down a couple of hundred (dollars), which I feel is probably more reasonable," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden.
"For now, London is certainly going to go lower but...it was only Tuesday last week that we were down at $2,200. We're just giving up gains of a couple of trading sessions ago," he said.
Citing a Fibonacci retracement from the April lows up to last week's peak of $2,670, Haylor said July robustas were likely to edge lower towards the 50-percent level placed around a gap at $2,240.

But fundamentally, analysts said while both markets would be prone to hefty bouts of profit-taking the overall uptrend would remain intact -- especially if there were frost fears in Brazil in the coming weeks.
"I think one can start asking questions about whether that's the end of the bull market later," Haylor said.
According to independent forecaster Weather Services Corp, no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee-growing areas.
Monday and Tuesday would be dry, with temperatures near to above normal, while the outlook was for a chance of a few light showers on Wednesday and generally dry conditions on Thursday and Friday.
Temperatures would be near to above normal, WSC said.
